transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2028-05-06 16:00 UTC
- Duration: ~42 minutes
- Attendees: Aisha Patel (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Evan Cho (Delta Nexus CTO), Rita Singh (ML Platform Lead), Tom Alvarez (Infra)

Auto-summary:
Delta Nexus is evaluating options to move from a primarily OpenAI-based hosted setup into a more cost-predictable deployment. They want to understand tradeoffs between Redwood hosted, dedicated reserved capacity, and a private VPC/on-prem package. Primary concerns: latency at 95th percentile for inference, unit token cost, data residency and KMS, auditability (audit logs), and model compatibility (vLLM/TGI parity, tokenizer/kv cache compatibility). Action: Redwood to share benchmark runbook, security docs, and a pilot quote; Delta Nexus to share usage logs and sample prompt sets.

Topics covered:
- Current architecture and pain points (OpenAI usage patterns, bursty nightly batch jobs)
- Perf and cost targets (50ms median, 200ms p95 for chat; reduce per-token spend by ~35%)
- Hosting options: Redwood Hosted API vs Dedicated reserved GPU pool vs Private VPC/on-prem
- Compatibility: vLLM / TGI model artifacts, tokenizer issues, KV cache behavior
- Security/compliance: SOC2, ISO, SSO/SAML, KMS/HSM, audit logs retention
- Next steps and pilot scoping

Transcript:
[00:00] Aisha (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. quick intros, then we want to understand your current stack and what success looks like.
[00:18] Evan (Delta Nexus): sure, uh thanks. i'm evan, cto. main goal for us is to get costs under control — openai is nice but it's getting pricey for the scaling we're doing. also we need more control for data residency.
[00:35] Rita (Delta Nexus): rita here, i run ml platform. we run a mix of synchronous chat endpoints and a bunch of asynchronous batch generation overnight. the overnight jobs spike tokens and blow out budgets.
[00:48] Tom (Delta Nexus): tom, infra. our security folks want KMS for keys, audit logs, and some network isolation — ideally VPC.
[00:59] Marco (Redwood): got it. so high level: we have three rails — hosted api, dedicated reserved pools, and private (vpc / on-prem). hosted is fastest to onboard. dedicated gives you predictable throughput and isolation. private gives full networking control.
[01:18] Evan: what does dedicated exactly buy us vs hosted? like will latency be the same?
[01:27] Aisha: great question. dedicated gives you reserved GPU capacity so you avoid noisy neighbor. you'll get guarantees on throughput and more predictable p95 latency. hosted is multi-tenant so you might see more variance at scale, although we do autoscale.
[01:43] Rita: for us p95 is critical. if an end-user waits >200 ms for a chat token, we get complaints. median is fine but p95 matters.
[01:55] Marco: our typical p95 on dedicated pools for Llama-like models at 8k context is in the low 100s ms for streaming tokens, but depends on batching and KV cache hit rates. i should caveat that tokenizer differences between models and vllm/TGI runtimes can change numbers — sometimes transcribed as kv cash in logs — uh kv cache.
[02:18] Evan: right — we're running a mix of tgi-backed hosts and vLLM internally, and we tried to port some of the fine-tunes. compatibility was rough — tokenization differences threw off our eval parity.
[02:33] Aisha: ok that's important. part of our onboarding is a model-compat matrix and a small parity eval to check outputs. marco can run a vllm/TGI compatibility pass and we can map tokenizers and checkpoint names.
[02:46] Marco: yeah i'll need the model artifacts or a docker pull URL; also the tokenizer config and a few sample prompts. that helps us reproduce the delta.
[02:57] Rita: we have a weird issue where prompts that worked on openai chat completions change length when tokenized under our local tokenizer, so the batching and cost estimates go off.
[03:12] Aisha: makes sense — we'll include a tokenizer diff checklist in the runbook.

[03:26] (minor crosstalk)
[03:34] Evan: on security — SOC2 is a blocker. we also need SSO, SAML for RBAC and per-route audit logs. can your private option do HSM-backed keys?
[03:49] Marco: yes for private we integrate with customer KMS/HSM and can surface key rotation policies. hosted supports envelope encryption with customer-managed keys via our KMS integrations, but private gives you direct control.
[04:04] Tom: what about logging retention? our compliance requires 12 months of audit logs with immutable storage.
[04:12] Aisha: we can extend retention on the console/observability plan or push logs to your SIEM via syslog/forwarders. we'll send the specifics.

[04:30] Rita: one thing — we sometimes fallback to smaller models to save cost during heavy load, is that supported?
[04:38] Marco: yes called smart routing; you can set policies to route by latency or cost and auto-fallback to a cheaper variant if p95 exceeds threshold. it's config driven.
[04:50] Evan: can we do A/B style rollouts? we want to test openai parity vs a local small-quant model slowly.
[04:58] Aisha: absolutely, per-route rollouts, traffic splits, canary. we'll document the rollback triggers.

[05:12] (pause)
[05:20] Rita: on cost, whats the unit economics — per-token on hosted vs dedicated? we need order-of-magnitude to decide.
[05:28] Aisha: hosted is pay-as-you-go with per-token plus infra margin. dedicated is committed monthly — you get lower per-token due to reserved GPUs and better batching. we'll send illustrative cost models. for example, depending on model and batch shapes, dedicated can be 20-40% cheaper at our sample workloads.
[05:48] Tom: do you support GPU types? we use A100s today but might consider H100 for futher throughput.
[05:57] Marco: yes, we run multiple instance types; for private we can match your on-prem GPUs, and dedicated pools can be configured to H100 where available. kernel selection and quantization affect throughput.

[06:16] Evan: about parity — our internal evals showed small but consistent differences when moving off openai -> vllm. we need a regression alert tied to a prompt set.
[06:27] Marco: we have eval hooks and monitoring to compare outputs and signal regressions. we can tie alerts to a prompt set and do regression deltas based on BLEU/ROUGE or semantic sims, whatever you use.
[06:42] Rita: good — and can you run a warm-up to prime the kv cache so our latency numbers are realistic?
[06:48] Marco: yes, warm-up + prefix caching is part of the perf run. caching usually reduces p95 significantly for repeat prefixes.

[07:02] Evan: what about data residency? some customers require EU-only or on-prem.
[07:08] Aisha: for hosted we have region controls; dedicated can be provisioned in a region for better data locality; private gives you full control.

[07:20] Rita: we have a procurement timeline — security signoff in 6 weeks, pilot in 8-10 weeks. is that feasible?
[07:28] Aisha: yes that's doable. we'll prioritize the SOC2 docs and runbook so your security team can triage quickly.

[07:36] (background noise, brief mislabeling: speaker 1)
[07:44] Tom: on networking, if we go private what does the control plane look like? do we need to open egress?
[07:50] Marco: private can be customer-managed control plane. we support a reverse-proxy model for air-gapped; if you want fully on-prem, the package includes offline installers. for VPC we need a few allowed endpoints for updates/metrics; we'll lay out the network ports.

[08:10] Evan: approx how long to run a parity eval? we want a quick sanity check vs openai plus a deeper 2-week run for quantitative results.
[08:20] Marco: quick sanity 1-2 days for a smoke test with 1000 prompts. deeper run 10-14 days to get stable p95 numbers and cost distribution.

[08:34] Rita: do you have example prompt sets or should we provide ours?
[08:40] Aisha: please provide yours; we'll also provide a sample set. the more representative, the better.

[08:48] Evan: ok next steps then?
[08:51] Aisha: i'll send the benchmark runbook, request checklist for model artifacts (tokenizer, checkpoint refs), and pricing. marco will own the perf checklist. can we aim to have your usage logs by next tuesday?
[09:04] Evan: yes we can get last 30 days.

[09:10] Rita: also, is there any existing reference or case study for a customer who did an openai exit to you?
[09:17] Aisha: yes we'll link two short case studies — one with a retail customer who saved ~30% and one mid-market SaaS that moved to dedicated. i'll include the links in the follow-up.

[09:30] (short pause, wrap-up)
[09:36] Marco: small note — when you send token distributions, include median and 95th seq lengths. batching changes are very sensitive to seq length skew.
[09:46] Tom: noted.

[09:50] Aisha: great — i'll capture action items and follow-up. thanks all.
[09:55] Evan: thanks, appreciate it.

End notes: some transcribed terms may be imperfect — e.g., 'kv cash' instead of 'KV cache', 'v-L-M' for vLLM, 'Redwood Dedicate' for Dedicated. Shared artifacts: benchmark_runbook_v1.pdf (link in follow-up), cost_model_example.xlsx, SOC2_and_ISO_overview.pdf.
